title: Patronage Standing and the Per-Unit Retain on Stored Bushels
content:
Bushels held under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements may or may not earn the member patronage allocation, and where they do a capital retain is taken for each bushel stored and credited to the member's equity account. Both columns are posted programme by programme.

| Programme | Bushels earn patronage allocation | Per-unit retain (USD per bushel stored) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Storage Account | no | 0.0000 |
| Grain Bank Deposit Account | yes | 0.0020 |
| Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage | yes | 0.0020 |
| Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement | yes | 0.0020 |
| Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement | yes | 0.0020 |
| Identity Preserved Segregated Storage | yes | 0.0020 |

## Notes

Five of the six programmes in the catalogue earn patronage on the bushels stored under them, and each of those five posts the same per-unit retain of 0.0020 for each bushel. The Open Storage Account earns no patronage and posts a retain of nil.

The retain is capital retained for each bushel stored and credited to the member's own equity account; it is not a charge for a service performed on the grain.

## Illustration on a hypothetical quantity

Twenty-two thousand bushels standing under a Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement, a programme that earns patronage, carry the posted per-unit rate of 0.0020 for each bushel: twenty-two thousand multiplied by two thousandths of a dollar, which is 44.00 credited to the member's equity. The same bushels on an Open Storage Account carry nothing, that programme earning no patronage at all.
